q8.answer: The MERGE replaces a live row only when the staged row's updated_at is strictly later, and ignores a staged row whose updated_at is the same or older. Staging first reduces the extract to one row per order_id with the greatest updated_at, so duplicates from the 2-hour lookback or a rerun cannot overwrite a newer version.

q9.answer: The high-water mark is stored as hwm_updated_at (UTC) in the single etl_pipeline_state row in the warehouse, initialized to 1970-01-01. It is written to the greater of the old HWM and the largest updated_at among the staged rows, in the same warehouse transaction as the MERGE and the run-log commit, so it moves only when that transaction commits. An empty window leaves it unchanged.

q10.answer: Dashboards read only the live orders table, and the MERGE, the HWM update and the etl_run_log committed mark all happen in one warehouse transaction. Readers see the previous night until COMMIT and the new night afterward, and staging tables are never read by readers. A failed or rolled-back attempt leaves orders unchanged. This relies on the warehouse giving standard transaction isolation, which I had listed as a confirmation item to check.

q11.answer: The failed attempt's staging table stays in the warehouse for debugging and is never reused, and its transaction was rolled back so none of its rows reached orders. The retry writes to its own stg_orders_D_attemptN+1 table and computes a fresh window from the unchanged HWM, so it extracts the same H minus 2 hours window as the failed attempt.

q12.answer: Reconciliation re-reads every row from the replica whose created_at falls on the mismatched creation day, not just rows in the nightly window. It stages them and MERGEs them into orders in one transaction using the same later-updated_at rule, then re-compares and logs the result. The high-water mark is not touched.
